+# Manage intelligent call delegation in Microsoft Teams - Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Learn
+
+**APPLIES TO:**![Image of an x for No](/en-us/office/media/icons/cancel-teams.png)Meetings ![Image of an x for No](/en-us/office/media/icons/cancel-teams.png)Events ![Image of a checkmark for Yes](/en-us/office/media/icons/success-teams.png)Calls
+
+Note
+
+This feature is currently in public preview.
+
+## Overview
+
+Intelligent call delegation in Microsoft Teams is an AI-powered voice agent that helps users manage incoming calls. It answers calls on users' behalf, gathers context about the caller's intent, and takes action based on users' availability and settings. It can screen calls, route urgent calls to users, and schedule follow-up appointments through Microsoft Bookings.
+
+As an admin, you use Teams personal attendant policies to control whether users in your organization can use intelligent call delegation, and which settings are available to them.
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+- Users must have a Microsoft Copilot license.
+- Intelligent call delegation uses usage-based billing with Copilot Credits. Admins must [set up usage-based billing for Copilot Credits](/en-us/copilot/implement/usage-based-billing-copilot-credits-setup) and [create a spending policy](/en-us/copilot/implement/usage-based-billing-manage-copilot-credits) for intelligent call delegation in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
+
+    Note
+
+    When you create the spending policy, under **Agents and services**, ensure that only **Intelligent call delegation** is selected. Clear the checkboxes for all other services. When you select users and groups, choose the appropriate scope before assigning the policy.
+
+## How intelligent call delegation works
+
+When users turn on intelligent call delegation, the voice agent answers calls on their behalf. Depending on the user's settings, it can perform actions including:
+
+- Screen incoming calls and collect the caller's reason for calling.
+- Route urgent calls to the user and provide context about the call.
+- Route suspected spam calls to voicemail when spam filtering is enabled.
+- Schedule callbacks and follow-up meetings when the user is unavailable, including after the user returns from out of office.
+- Notify the user when it answers or takes action on a call. Users can monitor calls through a live preview and join at any time.
+- Provide a post-call summary in call history when available.
+
+Callers are informed that they're speaking with an attendant rather than a person. When intelligent call delegation is turned on, it replaces the user's existing call routing settings. For more information about the user experience, see [Use intelligent call delegation in Microsoft Teams](https://support.microsoft.com/teams/copilot/use-copilot-call-delegation-in-microsoft-teams).
+
+## Manage intelligent call delegation
+
+You can use the Teams admin center or PowerShell to manage intelligent call delegation for your users. By default, intelligent call delegation is enabled in Teams personal attendant policy, and users with the policy can choose whether to turn it on or off in their Teams settings. Individual settings, such as call screening and scheduling follow-ups, are also enabled by default, and users can change them. Depending on the setting, users can turn it on or off or choose from available options.
+
+### Use the Teams admin center
+
+1. In the left navigation of the Teams admin center, go to **Voice** > **Personal attendant policies**.
+2. Select an existing policy or create a new one.
+3. Under **General**, turn **Enable Personal Attendant** on or off.
+4. If you turned on **Enable Personal Attendant**, configure the remaining policy settings under the following sections:
+
+    - **Choose how Personal Attendant speaks**
+    - **Choose which calls Personal Attendant answers**
+    - **Choose what Personal Attendant can do**
+    - **Manage recording and transcription**
+
+    For more information about each policy setting, see the Policy settings table.
+5. Select **Save**.
+
+#### Policy settings
+
+The following table describes personal attendant policy settings for intelligent call delegation in the Teams admin center.
+
+| Policy setting | Description |
+| --- | --- |
+| **Choose how Personal Attendant speaks** |  |
+| User's preferred name | Specifies the name Personal Attendant uses when referring to the user. |
+| Assistant voice | Specifies the voice callers hear when Personal Attendant answers calls. |
+| Language | Specifies the language Personal Attendant uses to communicate with callers. |
+| Conversation tone | Specifies the tone Personal Attendant uses when communicating with callers. |
+| **Choose which calls Personal Attendant answers** |  |
+| Internal Teams calls | Controls whether Personal Attendant answers calls from users in the same organization. |
+| Federated Teams calls | Controls whether Personal Attendant answers calls from other organizations. |
+| External PSTN calls | Controls whether Personal Attendant answers calls from the public telephone network. |
+| **Choose what Personal Attendant can do** |  |
+| Screen calls before connecting | Controls whether Personal Attendant screens calls and provides context before connecting. |
+| Calendar integration | Controls whether Personal Attendant can access the user's personal Bookings calendar to check availability and schedule follow-ups. |
+| Callbacks for people outside the user's contacts | Controls whether Personal Attendant uses calendar integration for callbacks to people outside the user's contacts. |
+| **Manage recording and transcription** |  |
+| Automatically save transcription | Controls whether transcripts are automatically saved for calls handled by Personal Attendant. |
+| Automatically save recording | Controls whether recordings are automatically saved for calls handled by Personal Attendant. |
+
+### Use PowerShell
+
+Use the following PowerShell cmdlets to create, manage, and assign personal attendant policies:
+
+- [New-CsTeamsPersonalAttendantPolicy](/en-us/powershell/module/microsoftteams/new-csteamspersonalattendantpolicy)
+- [Set-CsTeamsPersonalAttendantPolicy](/en-us/powershell/module/microsoftteams/set-csteamspersonalattendantpolicy)
+- [Get-CsTeamsPersonalAttendantPolicy](/en-us/powershell/module/microsoftteams/get-csteamspersonalattendantpolicy)
+- [Grant-CsTeamsPersonalAttendantPolicy](/en-us/powershell/module/microsoftteams/grant-csteamspersonalattendantpolicy)
+- [Remove-CsTeamsPersonalAttendantPolicy](/en-us/powershell/module/microsoftteams/remove-csteamspersonalattendantpolicy)
+
+Example:
+
+The following command creates a new policy named SalesPersonalAttendantPolicy with calendar integration for scheduling follow-ups disabled.
+
+```powershell
+New-CsTeamsPersonalAttendantPolicy -Identity SalesPersonalAttendantPolicy -CalendarBookings Disabled
+```
\ No newline at end of file

+# Personal voicemail AI triage billing - Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Learn
+
+This article is for IT pros and Teams administrators who want to set up usage-based billing for personal voicemail AI triage.
+
+Important
+
+This feature is available only through the Microsoft Frontier Program. General availability (GA) timing hasn't been announced yet.
+
+## Planning and licensing review
+
+### Planning
+
+- [Usage-based billing](/en-us/copilot/implement/usage-based-billing-copilot-credits-setup)
+- [Configure billing methods](/en-us/copilot/implement/usage-based-billing-copilot-credits-setup#configure-billing-method)
+
+### Licensing
+
+Personal voicemail AI triage requires:
+
+- A Microsoft 365 Copilot license for each user.
+- Usage-based billing.
+
+## Personal voicemail AI triage usage-based billing
+
+Each personal voicemail is charged once per processed voicemail.
+
+If you want to enable personal voicemail AI triage for all eligible users, use the **All users** option in spending policy scope.
+
+If you want to limit which users have personal voicemail AI triage enabled, create a Microsoft 365 security group and use the **Specific groups** option in the spending policy scope. To apply different spending limits to different users, create separate security groups. Limit the number of people who own these security groups.
+
+Configuring a spending policy alone doesn't enable AI triage for users. AI triage must also be enabled in voicemail policy.
+
+### For **Specific groups** option create a Microsoft 365 security group
+
+1. In the [Microsoft 365 admin center](https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/p/?linkid=2024339), go to **Teams & groups** > **Active teams and groups** > **Security groups**.
+2. Select **Add a security group**.
+3. Complete group setup and create the group.
+
+and Add users to the group
+
+1. Open the security group you created.
+2. Add owners.
+3. Add users who should be included in this policy.
+
+## Create a spending policy
+
+These steps require the **AI Administrator** role.
+
+### Add spending policy
+
+1. In the Microsoft 365 admin center, go to **Copilot** > **Cost Management**.
+2. Select the **Configuration** tab.
+3. Select **+ Add spending policy**.
+
+### Agents and services
+
+1. Turn off **Allow new Agents and services as they become available**.
+2. Select only **AI Triage for Personal Voicemail**.
+3. Clear all other services.
+4. Select **Next**.
+
+### Access scope
+
+1. Name the policy.
+2. Select one of the following:
+    - **Specific groups** to limit applicable users, and then select the Microsoft 365 security groups that contain the users.
+    - **All users** to apply the policy to all eligible users.
+3. Select **Next**.
+
+### Set limits and alerts
+
+1. Configure monthly spending limits.
+2. Optionally configure per-user limits.
+3. Optionally configure policy-level and user-level alerts.
+4. Select **Next**.
+
+### Billing method
+
+1. Use the default spending policy billing method, or override it if you're a Global admin or Billing admin.
+2. Select **Next**.
+
+### Review and add the policy
+
+1. Verify scope, services, billing method, limits, and alerts.
+2. Select **Create spending policy**.
+
+## Activation prerequisites and charging behavior
+
+Personal voicemail AI triage runs only when all of the following are true:
+
+- The user has a Microsoft 365 Copilot license.
+- A spending policy for **AI Triage for Personal Voicemail** is configured for that user in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
+- **Personal voicemail AI triage** is enabled in [Voicemail policies](manage-voicemail-policies) in the Teams admin center.
+
+If any requirement isn't met, AI triage isn't performed and no usage-based billing charges are incurred.
\ No newline at end of file

+# Shared voicemail AI triage billing - Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Learn
+
+This article is for IT pros and Teams administrators who want to set up usage-based billing for shared voicemail AI triage.
+
+Important
+
+This feature is available only through the Microsoft Frontier Program. General availability (GA) timing hasn't been announced yet.
+
+## Planning and licensing review
+
+### Planning
+
+- [Usage-based billing](/en-us/copilot/implement/usage-based-billing-copilot-credits-setup)
+- [Configure billing methods](/en-us/copilot/implement/usage-based-billing-copilot-credits-setup#configure-billing-method)
+
+### Licensing
+
+- Shared voicemail AI triage requires usage-based billing.
+- A Microsoft 365 Copilot license isn't required for shared voicemail triage.
+- For Queues app scenarios, the Queues app has separate licensing requirements (Teams Premium).
+
+## Shared voicemail AI triage usage-based billing
+
+Each shared voicemail is charged once per processed voicemail, regardless of how many users receive it.
+
+If you want to enable shared voicemail AI triage for all resource accounts, use the **All users** option in spending policy scope. This approach is recommended when you want to enable AI triage for all shared voicemail in your organization.
+
+If you want to limit which resource accounts have voicemail AI triage enabled, create a Microsoft 365 security group and use the **Specific groups** option in the spending policy scope. To apply different spending limits to different resource accounts, create separate security groups. Limit the number of people who own these security groups.
+
+Configuring a spending policy alone doesn't enable AI triage for resource accounts. AI triage must also be enabled in the specific Call Queue, Auto Attendant, and Teams Phone Agent templates.
+
+### For "Specific groups" option create a Microsoft 365 security group
+
+1. In the [Microsoft 365 admin center](https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/p/?linkid=2024339), go to **Teams & groups** > **Active teams and groups** > **Security groups**.
+2. Select **Add a security group**.
+3. Complete group setup and create the group.
+
+and add Call Queue, Auto Attendant, and Teams Phone Agent resource accounts to the group
+
+1. Open the security group you created.
+2. Add owners.
+3. Add the resource accounts used by Auto Attendants, Call Queues, or Teams Phone Agents.
+
+## Create a spending policy
+
+These steps require the **AI Administrator** role.
+
+### Add spending policy
+
+1. In the Microsoft 365 admin center, go to **Copilot** > **Cost Management**.
+2. Select the **Configuration** tab.
+3. Select **+ Add spending policy**.
+
+### Agents and services
+
+1. Turn off **Allow new Agents and services as they become available**.
+2. Select only **AI Triage for Shared Voicemail**.
+3. Clear all other services.
+4. Select **Next**.
+
+### Access scope
+
+1. Name the policy.
+2. Select one of the following:
+    - **Specific groups** to limit applicable Call Queue, Auto Attendant, and Teams Phone Agent resource accounts, and then select the Microsoft 365 security groups that contain these resource accounts.
+    - **All users** to apply the policy to all resource accounts.
+3. Select **Next**.
+
+### Set limits and alerts
+
+1. Configure monthly spending limits.
+2. Optionally configure per-resource-account limits.
+3. Optionally configure policy-level and user-level alerts.
+4. Select **Next**.
+
+### Billing method
+
+1. Use the default spending policy billing method, or override it if you're a Global admin or Billing admin.
+2. Select **Next**.
+
+### Review and add the policy
+
+1. Verify scope, services, billing method, limits, and alerts.
+2. Select **Create spending policy**.
+
+## Activation prerequisites and charging behavior
+
+Shared voicemail AI triage runs only when both are true:
+
+- A spending policy is configured for **AI Triage for Shared Voicemail** for the applicable resource account in Microsoft 365 admin center.
+- An "AI triage for shared voicemails" template is selected under the specific Auto Attendant, Call Queue, or Teams Phone Agent settings in Teams admin center.
+
+If no template is selected, AI triage isn't performed and no usage-based billing charges are incurred, even when a spending policy is configured.
+
+## Billing attribution
+
+Shared voicemail AI triage is billed once per processed voicemail, regardless of how many users receive the voicemail.
+
+The charge is attributed to the resource account associated with the Auto Attendant, Call Queue, or Teams Phone Agent. If an Auto Attendant or Call Queue doesn't have its own resource account, the root resource account associated with the phone number is used for billing.
\ No newline at end of file

+# Automatic voicemail triage with AI - Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Learn
+
+Automatic voicemail triage uses a compliant and secure Large Language Model (LLM) to help users interpret and prioritize voicemail messages through transcript analysis.
+
+When enabled, the system can generate:
+
+- A concise summary of the message.
+- Categories and priority indicators.
+- Suggested follow-up actions.
+- Highlighted key terms for quick review.
+
+Important
+
+This feature is available only through the Microsoft Frontier Program. General availability (GA) timing hasn't been announced yet.
+
+## How voicemail triage works
+
+Voicemail triage runs after a message is recorded and before it's delivered to Exchange.
+
+The service analyzes the voicemail transcript and can generate these outputs:
+
+- **Summary**: A concise, natural-language paragraph that starts with the caller's intent and includes key details (for example, dates, times, requested actions, or contact information).
+- **Category**: A topic label for the voicemail. Some categories are system-defined (for example, junk and harmful content), and other categories are generated from transcript content.
+- **Suggested actions**: Recommended follow-up tasks derived from the voicemail content. System-defined action labels include callback, set appointment, reschedule appointment, cancel appointment, and email reply, followed by other requested actions generated from the transcript.
+- **Importance flag (urgency)**: A priority signal for time-critical messages, which can mark the voicemail as important in Outlook.
+
+Generated triage insights are stored with the voicemail in Exchange and can be used by downstream automations such as Outlook rules, agent-based workflows, and other LLM-powered processes.
+
+If AI-generated content doesn't appear for a voicemail, audio or transcript clarity might be insufficient for reliable triage output.
+
+## Scope
+
+- **Shared voicemail triage** applies to missed calls handled by Auto Attendants, Call Queues, and Teams Phone Agents.
+- **Personal voicemail triage** applies to a user's personal Teams voicemail.
+
+For shared voicemail, AI triage data is also shown in the Teams Queues app experience. This Queues app experience isn't generally available (GA) yet. The Queues app requires a Teams Premium license.
+
+## Admin controls
+
+Admins can control which AI outputs are generated:
+
+- For **personal voicemail**, configure user settings in the Teams admin center (**Manage users** > **Voicemail** > **Personal voicemail AI triage**) or by using PowerShell.
+- For **shared voicemail**, configure settings in the **AI triage of shared voicemails** template used by Auto Attendants, Call Queues, and Teams Phone Agents in the Teams admin center or by using PowerShell.
+
+## Requirements
+
+### Personal voicemail triage
+
+Personal voicemail triage requires all of the following:
+
+- A Microsoft 365 Copilot license for the user.
+- A spending policy for **AI Triage for Personal Voicemail** configured in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
+- Voicemail AI triage enabled in [Voicemail policies](manage-voicemail-policies) in the Teams admin center.
+
+If any requirement isn't met, AI triage isn't performed and no usage-based billing charges are incurred.
+
+### Shared voicemail triage
+
+Shared voicemail triage requires both of the following:
+
+- A spending policy for **AI Triage for Shared Voicemail** configured for the applicable resource account in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
+- A **Voicemail AI triage template** selected for the specific Auto Attendant, Call Queue, or Teams Phone Agent in the Teams admin center.
+
+If no template is selected, AI triage isn't performed and no usage-based billing charges are incurred, even when a spending policy is configured.
+
+## Billing summary
+
+Billing is per voicemail processed:
+
+- **Personal voicemail triage**: Charged per voicemail processed. For configuration details, see [Personal voicemail AI triage billing](personal-voicemail-ai-triage-billing).
+- **Shared voicemail triage**: Charged once per voicemail processed, even when the same voicemail is delivered to multiple users. For configuration details, see [Shared voicemail AI triage billing](shared-voicemail-ai-triage-billing).
+
+For shared voicemail, cost is attributed to the resource account associated with the Auto Attendant, Call Queue, or Teams Phone Agent. If an Auto Attendant or Call Queue doesn't have its own resource account, billing uses the root resource account associated with the phone number.
+
+## Availability
+
+During TAP and early GA, voicemail AI triage is available only for tenants whose tenant language is set to English.
+
+Additional languages and organization-defined custom categories and suggested actions might be introduced based on customer demand and feedback.
\ No newline at end of file

messageCenterItems.title: Microsoft Teams: Intelligent call recap for call queues in the Queues app on mobile
messageCenterItems.summary: Microsoft Teams mobile's Queues app will add intelligent call recap for recorded and transcribed call queue calls starting early December 2026. Users can view AI-generated notes, key points, and follow-up tasks without replaying calls. No admin action is needed, but recording, transcription, and licenses should be confirmed.
messageCenterItems.body:
What and why

We're introducing intelligent call recap for call queue calls in the Queues app on Microsoft Teams mobile. This update extends the experience already available on desktop, allowing calling representatives and supervisors to review AI-generated notes, key discussion points, and recommended follow-up tasks without replaying recordings or reading full transcripts.

Rollout schedule

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Beginning in early December 2026 and expected to complete by mid-December 2026

Impact on your organization

Who is affected

  • Calling representatives and supervisors who use the Queues app on Microsoft Teams mobile and have access to recorded and transcribed call queue calls

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Teams mobile
  • Queues app

What will happen

After rollout:

  • Users can open a recorded call from shared call history and select View recap to review AI-generated notes, key discussion points, and recommended follow-up tasks.

Screenshot 1: 

Screenshot 2:

Screenshot 3:

  • Recap is available only for recorded and transcribed call queue calls and to users who already have access to the recording.
  • The feature does not change how call recordings are created, stored, or accessed.

Action required and recommendations

No admin action is required before rollout.

We recommend that you:

  • Confirm that recording and transcription are enabled for call queues where you want users to access intelligent call recap.
  • Review license assignments for users who will use the feature.

Learn more

  • Intelligent recap for Teams calls, meetings, and events - Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Learn

Compliance considerations

Organizations should review their existing recording, transcription, and AI-related compliance requirements as appropriate.

messageCenterItems.title: Microsoft Teams: External presenter support for event group chat
messageCenterItems.summary: Microsoft Teams will support external presenters in event group chat starting late March 2027. This allows external presenters to join and coordinate in event chats if "Enable Green room" and external collaboration are enabled. The change introduces cross-tenant chat without storing new customer data.
messageCenterItems.body:
Updated November 18, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

What and why

We are adding support for external presenters in event group chat, the private chat used by organizers, co-organizers, and presenters for coordination during an event or structured meeting. This change enables presenters who are outside the tenant hosting the meeting or event to participate in the event group chat.

Rollout schedule

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Rollout will begin in late March 2027 (previously early December 2026) and is expected to complete by mid-April 2027 (previously early January).

Impact on your organization

Who is affected

  • Organizers, co-organizers, and presenters using event group chat in meetings or events, including external presenters.

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Teams
  • Event group chat
  • Meetings and events with the Enable Green room Teams meeting option enabled

What will happen

  • External presenters will be able to join the event group chat used for coordination during a meeting or event.
  • The meeting or event must have the Enable Green room Teams meeting option enabled to use event group chat. 
  • External user collaboration must be enabled for external presenters to use this functionality.

Action required and recommendations

If your organization wants external presenters to use event group chat, ensure external user collaboration is enabled in Teams admin center > External collaboration.

Compliance considerations

Does the change store new customer data?

  • No. Expected changes on the client will only correct the tenantId to the external federated presenter's own tenant.

Does the change alter how existing customer data is processed, stored, or accessed (e.g., documents, emails, chats, etc.)?

  • Yes. External federated presenters can now read and post in the event group chat. That includes messages written before they joined, if the thread shows history. The presenter's stored tenantId also changes from the organizer's tenant to the presenter's own tenant.

Does the change provide a new way of communicating between users, tenants, or subscriptions?

  • Yes. We are adding a new cross-tenant chat path between the organizer's tenant and external presenters. Both tenants must allow external access.

Does the change modify how users can access, export, delete, or correct their personal data within Microsoft 365 services (GDPR Data Subject Rights)?

  • No. External presenters' messages fall under existing federated-chat handling.

messageCenterItems.title: Microsoft Teams: End of support for iOS 17 and iPadOS 17
messageCenterItems.summary: Microsoft Teams will end support for iOS 17 and iPadOS 17 starting mid-December 2026, requiring iOS/iPadOS 18 or later for new releases. Existing versions will keep working without support. Organizations should notify users, encourage OS upgrades, update policies, and revise support documentation accordingly.
messageCenterItems.body:
What and Why:

Microsoft Teams is ending support for upcoming builds on iOS 17 and iPadOS 17. As this change rolls out, new Teams releases will require iOS 18 or later on iPhone and iPadOS 18 or later on iPad.

Rollout Schedule:

General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out in mid-December 2026 and expect to complete by early January 2027.

Impact on Your Organization:

Users whose devices remain on iOS 17 or iPadOS 17 will not be able to install newer Teams releases that require a newer operating system.

Teams versions already installed on these devices will continue functioning without official support. This change does not introduce a block on opening or signing in to those existing installations.

Action Required/Recommendations:

  • Identify devices running iOS 17 or iPadOS 17 and notify affected users.
  • Advise users to upgrade to a supported operating system, then update Teams through the Apple App Store, to continue receiving supported Teams releases.
  • Review any mobile device management (MDM) or app deployment policies that pin or require specific iOS/iPadOS versions, and update them to allow iOS 18/iPadOS 18 so affected devices are not blocked from upgrading.
  • Update internal support documentation and helpdesk guidance.

Learn more: Hardware requirements for Microsoft Teams.

Compliance considerations:

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.
